source.text: וַיַּֽעַשׂ־ל֥וֹ בָתִּ֖ים בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑יד וַיָּ֤כֶן מָקוֹם֙ לַֽאֲר֣וֹן הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיֶּט־ל֖וֹ אֹֽהֶל׃

records.literal_gloss: And made for himself houses in [the] city of David, and prepared a place for [the] ark of the God, and pitched for it a tent.

en.L: And he made houses for himself in the city of David, and he prepared a place for the ark of God and pitched a tent for it.
en.B: David built houses for himself in the city of David. He also prepared a place for the ark of God, and he pitched a tent for it.
en.R: David built houses for himself in the city of David. He also got a place ready for the ark of God and set up a tent for it.

decisions.choice: he: David
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject; it carries on from chapter 14, where David is settled in Jerusalem and Hiram of Tyre builds him a house (14:1-2).

decisions.choice: houses in the city of David: buildings for the king and his household
decisions.reason: The city of David was the stronghold of Zion that David had taken and named after himself (11:5-7). "Houses" may mean the rooms and buildings of his palace and those for his growing family (14:3).

decisions.choice: a tent for the ark: a new tent in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: David prepares a place and sets up a tent for the ark in his own city, as 2 Samuel 6:17 also says. It is not the old tent of meeting, which stayed at Gibeon (16:39; 21:29). After three months at the house of Obed-Edom (13:14), the ark now has a place ready for it.

decisions.choice: David built
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name David as the subject, and use "built" for the general verb "made", since houses are meant.

source.text: אָ֚ז אָמַ֣ר דָּוִ֔יד לֹ֤א לָשֵׂאת֙ אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים כִּ֖י אִם־הַלְוִיִּ֑ם כִּי־בָ֣ם׀בָּחַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה לָשֵׂ֞את אֶת־אֲר֧וֹן יְהוָ֛ה וּֽלְשָׁרְת֖וֹ עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Then said David, Not to carry the ark of the God except the Levites, for them chose Yahweh to carry [the] ark of Yahweh and to serve him until forever.

en.L: Then David said, "[No one is] to carry the ark of God except the Levites, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} chose them to carry the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and to serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} forever."
en.B: Then David said, "No one may carry the ark of God except the Levites, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} chose them to carry the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and to serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} forever."
en.R: Then David said, "Only the Levites may carry the ark of God. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} chose them to carry the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and to serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for all time."

decisions.choice: chose them to carry the ark and to serve him: the Levites' task in the law
decisions.reason: David repeats what Deuteronomy 10:8 says: the LORD set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the covenant and to stand before him to serve him. Numbers 1:50 and 4:15 give the carrying of the holy things to the Levites. On the first attempt the ark had been set on a cart (13:7), and Uzzah died (13:9-10); David now sees what went wrong (verse 13).

decisions.choice: not to carry ... except the Levites: a rule, no one else may carry it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "not to carry" with no subject, a short way of stating a rule. "Except" makes clear who alone may do it.

decisions.choice: to serve him forever: to minister to the LORD for all time
decisions.reason: The verb is used of service in worship by priests and Levites. "Him" is the LORD, as in Deuteronomy 10:8. "Forever" means the appointment is lasting, not for this one journey only.

decisions.choice: [No one is]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the subject the Hebrew leaves out, so the rule can be read as a sentence.

source.text: וַיַּקְהֵ֥ל דָּוִ֛יד אֶת־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל־יְרֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לְהַעֲלוֹת֙ אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־מְקוֹמ֖וֹ אֲשֶׁר־הֵכִ֥ין לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And assembled David all Israel to Jerusalem to bring up [the] ark of Yahweh to its place which he had prepared for it.

en.L: And David assembled all Israel at Jerusalem to bring up the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to its place, which he had prepared for it.
en.B: David assembled all Israel at Jerusalem to bring the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} up to the place he had prepared for it.
en.R: David called all Israel together in Jerusalem to bring the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} up to the place he had made ready for it.

decisions.choice: all Israel: the people gathered from the whole nation
decisions.reason: As in 13:5, "all Israel" means the nation represented by its people and leaders (verse 25), not every single person. Chronicles often stresses that the whole people took part.

decisions.choice: bring up: carry up to the higher city
decisions.reason: Jerusalem stood high in the hill country, so going there is "going up". The ark had been left at the house of Obed-Edom (13:13-14), and is now to be brought up to the place of verse 1.

decisions.choice: made ready
decisions.reason: Readable says "made ready" for "prepared", as in verse 1.

source.text: וַיֶּאֱסֹ֥ף דָּוִ֛יד אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י אַֽהֲרֹ֖ן וְאֶת־הַלְוִיִּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And gathered David [the] sons of Aaron and the Levites.

en.L: And David gathered the sons of Aaron and the Levites.
en.B: David gathered the sons of Aaron and the Levites.
en.R: David brought together the priests, who were Aaron's descendants, and the Levites.

decisions.choice: the sons of Aaron and the Levites: the priests and the rest of the tribe of Levi
decisions.reason: The priests were the descendants of Aaron. The other Levites assisted them and looked after the sanctuary and its holy things (Numbers 3:5-10). Both groups are called for the ark (verses 11 and 14).

decisions.choice: the priests, who were Aaron's descendants
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the sons of Aaron were the priests.

source.text: לִבְנֵ֖י קְהָ֑ת אוּרִיאֵ֣ל הַשָּׂ֔ר וְאֶחָ֖יו מֵאָ֥ה וְעֶשְׂרִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Of [the] sons of Kohath: Uriel the chief, and his brothers, 120.

en.L: Of the sons of Kohath: Uriel the chief, and his brothers, 120.
en.B: From the descendants of Kohath: Uriel the chief, and 120 of his relatives.
en.R: From the clan of Kohath came Uriel, their leader, and 120 of his relatives.

decisions.choice: Kohath: one of the three sons of Levi
decisions.reason: Levi's sons were Gershom, Kohath and Merari (6:1; Exodus 6:16), and the Levites were organized by these clans. The Kohathites had the task of carrying the most holy things, the ark among them (Numbers 4:4-15). Verses 5-10 name six groups; four of them (Kohath, Elizaphan, Hebron and Uzziel) are Kohathite.

decisions.choice: the chief: the head of the clan
decisions.reason: The word is used for any leader or official. Here it is the head of a Levite clan, who leads his kinsmen (verse 12 calls them "heads of the fathers' houses").

decisions.choice: his brothers: his fellow clansmen
decisions.reason: "Brothers" means the men of his clan, his relatives, not only his brothers by birth.

decisions.choice: chief (Literal, Balanced); leader (Readable)
decisions.reason: For a head of a Levite clan, "chief" fits better than the "princes" or "officials" used for this word at court. Readable says "their leader". The same choice is made in verses 6-10, 16 and 22.

decisions.choice: his relatives
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "relatives" for "brothers" (m3), and put the number before them.

source.text: לִבְנֵ֖י מְרָרִ֑י עֲשָׂיָ֣ה הַשָּׂ֔ר וְאֶחָ֖יו מָאתַ֥יִם וְעֶשְׂרִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Of [the] sons of Merari: Asaiah the chief, and his brothers, 220.

en.L: Of the sons of Merari: Asaiah the chief, and his brothers, 220.
en.B: From the descendants of Merari: Asaiah the chief, and 220 of his relatives.
en.R: From the clan of Merari came Asaiah, their leader, and 220 of his relatives.

decisions.choice: Merari: the third son of Levi
decisions.reason: The Merarites had carried the frames, bars, posts and bases of the tabernacle in the wilderness (Numbers 4:29-33). The rest of the record follows verse 5.

decisions.choice: chief; relatives
decisions.reason: As in verse 5.

source.text: לִבְנֵ֖י גֵּרְשׁ֑וֹם יוֹאֵ֣ל הַשָּׂ֔ר וְאֶחָ֖יו מֵאָ֥ה וּשְׁלֹשִֽׁים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Of [the] sons of Gershom: Joel the chief, and his brothers, 130.

en.L: Of the sons of Gershom: Joel the chief, and his brothers, 130.
en.B: From the descendants of Gershom: Joel the chief, and 130 of his relatives.
en.R: From the clan of Gershom came Joel, their leader, and 130 of his relatives.

decisions.choice: Gershom: the son of Levi called Gershon in the Law
decisions.reason: Exodus 6:16 and Numbers 3:17 spell the name Gershon. Chronicles uses the form Gershom here and in 6:1-2, and it is the same clan. The Gershonites had carried the curtains and coverings of the tabernacle (Numbers 4:24-28).

decisions.choice: chief; relatives
decisions.reason: As in verse 5.

source.text: לִבְנֵ֖י אֱלִֽיצָפָ֑ן שְׁמַֽעְיָ֥ה הַשָּׂ֖ר וְאֶחָ֥יו מָאתָֽיִם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Of [the] sons of Elizaphan: Shemaiah the chief, and his brothers, 200.

en.L: Of the sons of Elizaphan: Shemaiah the chief, and his brothers, 200.
en.B: From the descendants of Elizaphan: Shemaiah the chief, and 200 of his relatives.
en.R: From the clan of Elizaphan came Shemaiah, their leader, and 200 of his relatives.

decisions.choice: Elizaphan: a Kohathite whose descendants formed a family of their own
decisions.reason: Elizaphan son of Uzziel was the leader of the Kohathite clans in the wilderness (Numbers 3:30), and with his brother helped carry out the bodies of Nadab and Abihu (Leviticus 10:4, where the name is spelled Elzaphan). His descendants were by now large enough to be counted as a group of their own (also 2 Chronicles 29:13).

decisions.choice: chief; relatives
decisions.reason: As in verse 5.

source.text: לִבְנֵ֖י חֶבְר֑וֹן אֱלִיאֵ֥ל הַשָּׂ֖ר וְאֶחָ֥יו שְׁמוֹנִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Of [the] sons of Hebron: Eliel the chief, and his brothers, eighty.

en.L: Of the sons of Hebron: Eliel the chief, and his brothers, eighty.
en.B: From the descendants of Hebron: Eliel the chief, and eighty of his relatives.
en.R: From the clan of Hebron came Eliel, their leader, and eighty of his relatives.

decisions.choice: Hebron: a son of Kohath, not the town
decisions.reason: Hebron is named as a son of Kohath in Exodus 6:18 and 1 Chronicles 5:28. His descendants form one of the Kohathite groups.

decisions.choice: chief; relatives
decisions.reason: As in verse 5.

source.text: לִבְנֵ֖י עֻזִּיאֵ֑ל עַמִּינָדָ֣ב הַשָּׂ֔ר וְאֶחָ֕יו מֵאָ֖ה וּשְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Of [the] sons of Uzziel: Amminadab the chief, and his brothers, 112.

en.L: Of the sons of Uzziel: Amminadab the chief, and his brothers, 112.
en.B: From the descendants of Uzziel: Amminadab the chief, and 112 of his relatives.
en.R: From the clan of Uzziel came Amminadab, their leader, and 112 of his relatives.

decisions.choice: Uzziel: a son of Kohath
decisions.reason: Uzziel was a son of Kohath (Exodus 6:18) and the father of Elizaphan (verse 8). With Kohath, Elizaphan and Hebron, this makes four Kohathite groups out of six, the clan to whom the law gave the carrying of the ark (Numbers 4:15).

decisions.choice: Amminadab: a Levite, not the Amminadab of Judah
decisions.reason: The same name belongs to a man of Judah, the father of Nahshon (2:10), and to a Kohathite in 6:7. This Amminadab is the head of Uzziel's descendants.

decisions.choice: chief; relatives
decisions.reason: As in verse 5.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֣א דָוִ֔יד לְצָד֥וֹק וּלְאֶבְיָתָ֖ר הַכֹּֽהֲנִ֑ים וְלַלְוִיִּ֗ם לְאֽוּרִיאֵ֤ל עֲשָׂיָה֙ וְיוֹאֵ֣ל שְׁמַֽעְיָ֔ה וֶאֱלִיאֵ֖ל וְעַמִּינָדָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And called David to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, and to the Levites, to Uriel, Asaiah and Joel, Shemaiah and Eliel and Amminadab.

en.L: And David called for Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and for the Levites, for Uriel, Asaiah and Joel, Shemaiah and Eliel and Amminadab.
en.B: Then David summoned Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and the Levites Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel and Amminadab.
en.R: Then David sent for the priests Zadok and Abiathar and for the Levite leaders Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel and Amminadab.

decisions.choice: Zadok and Abiathar the priests: the two chief priests of David's reign
decisions.reason: The two are named together as priests under David in 2 Samuel 8:17; 15:24-29 and 20:25. Abiathar had escaped when Saul killed the priests of Nob and had joined David (1 Samuel 22:20-23).

decisions.choice: Uriel ... Amminadab: the six chiefs of verses 5-10
decisions.reason: The six Levites are the heads of the six groups just listed, in the same order.

decisions.choice: the Levite leaders
decisions.reason: Readable says that these Levites are the leaders named in verses 5-10.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֔ם אַתֶּ֛ם רָאשֵׁ֥י הָאָב֖וֹת לַלְוִיִּ֑ם הִֽתְקַדְּשׁוּ֙ אַתֶּ֣ם וַאֲחֵיכֶ֔ם וְהַֽעֲלִיתֶ֗ם אֵ֣ת אֲר֤וֹן יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל־הֲכִינ֖וֹתִי לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, You [are the] heads of the fathers of the Levites; consecrate yourselves, you and your brothers, and bring up [the] ark of Yahweh [the] God of Israel to [where] I have prepared for it.

en.L: And he said to them, "You [are] the heads of the fathers' [houses] of the Levites. Consecrate yourselves, you and your brothers, and bring up the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel to [the place] I have prepared for it.
en.B: He said to them, "You are the heads of the Levite families. Consecrate yourselves, you and your relatives, and bring the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, up to the place I have prepared for it.
en.R: He told them, "You are the leaders of the Levite families. You and your relatives must make yourselves holy. Then bring the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, up to the place I have made ready for it.

decisions.choice: heads of the fathers: heads of the ancestral families
decisions.reason: A "house of the fathers" was an extended family within a clan. These men lead their families and speak for them.

decisions.choice: consecrate yourselves: make yourselves holy, ready to handle holy things
decisions.reason: To consecrate oneself was to prepare for coming near to what is holy, by washing, clean clothes and keeping away from what makes one unclean (Exodus 19:10-15, 22; Joshua 3:5).

decisions.choice: and bring up: a command
decisions.reason: The verb form continues the command "consecrate yourselves": first they are to make themselves holy, then they are to bring up the ark.

decisions.choice: fathers' [houses]; [the place]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the words the Hebrew leaves to be understood.

decisions.choice: make yourselves holy
decisions.reason: Readable says what "consecrate" means.

source.text: כִּ֛י לְמַ בָּרִ֥אשׁוֹנָ֖הלֹ֣א אַתֶּ֑ם פָּרַ֨ץ יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ בָּ֔נוּ כִּי־לֹ֥א דְרַשְׁנֻ֖הוּ כַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃

records.literal_gloss: For because at the first [time] not you, broke out Yahweh our God against us, for not we sought him according to the rule.

en.L: For because at the first [time] you [did] not [carry it], {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God broke out against us, because we did not seek {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} according to the rule."
en.B: It was because you did not carry it the first time that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God burst out against us, since we did not seek {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as the rule required."
en.R: The first time, you did not carry it, and so {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God burst out against us. We did not seek {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had commanded."

decisions.choice: because the first time you did not: you Levites did not carry the ark
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is very short: "because at the first, not you". From verses 2 and 12 the sense is that the Levites were not the ones who carried the ark on the first attempt, when it was set on a cart (13:7).

decisions.choice: the LORD broke out against us: the death of Uzzah
decisions.reason: David looks back to 13:9-11 (2 Samuel 6:6-8), when the LORD broke out against Uzzah and the place was named Perez-uzza, "breaking out against Uzza". The same verb is used here, and David now says "against us": the fault was the whole people's.

decisions.choice: we did not seek him: we did not turn to the LORD in the way he required
alternatives: we did not seek it (the ark) according to the rule
decisions.reason: To "seek" the LORD is to turn to him, ask his will and worship him. "Him" is most naturally the LORD just named. The same suffix could mean "it", the ark, as in 13:3, where David says they had not sought the ark in the days of Saul.

decisions.choice: according to the rule: as the law laid down
decisions.reason: The word means a ruling or ordinance, the right way something is to be done. The law said that the Kohathite Levites were to carry the holy things on their shoulders and must not touch them (Numbers 4:15; 7:9).

decisions.choice: did not carry it
decisions.reason: Every level supplies "carry it" (in brackets at Literal), the action the short Hebrew leaves to be understood (m1).

decisions.choice: in the way he had commanded
decisions.reason: Readable says "in the way he had commanded" for "according to the rule", since the rule is the one the LORD gave through Moses (verse 15).

source.text: וַיִּֽתְקַדְּשׁ֔וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֑ם לְהַעֲל֕וֹת אֶת־אֲר֥וֹן יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And consecrated themselves the priests and the Levites to bring up [the] ark of Yahweh [the] God of Israel.

en.L: And the priests and the Levites consecrated themselves to bring up the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel.
en.B: So the priests and the Levites consecrated themselves in order to bring up the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.
en.R: So the priests and the Levites made themselves holy, so that they could bring up the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: consecrated themselves: they did what David told them
decisions.reason: The verse uses the same verb as David's command in verse 12; the priests and Levites obey.

decisions.choice: made themselves holy
decisions.reason: As in verse 12.

source.text: וַיִּשְׂא֣וּ בְנֵֽי־הַלְוִיִּ֗ם אֵ֚ת אֲר֣וֹן הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה מֹשֶׁ֖ה כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה בִּכְתֵפָ֥ם בַּמֹּט֖וֹת עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And carried [the] sons of the Levites the ark of the God as commanded Moses according to [the] word of Yahweh, on their shoulder, with the poles on them.

en.L: And the sons of the Levites carried the ark of God, as Moses had commanded according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, on their shoulders, with the poles on them.
en.B: The Levites carried the ark of God with the poles on their shoulders, as Moses had commanded by the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Then the Levites carried the ark of God on their shoulders, using the poles, just as Moses had commanded. This was what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said.

decisions.choice: as Moses had commanded according to the word of the LORD: the law for carrying the ark
decisions.reason: The ark had rings and poles so that it could be carried (Exodus 25:13-15), and the Kohathites were to carry the holy things on their shoulders (Numbers 4:15; 7:9). Moses gave the command, but it was the LORD's word.

decisions.choice: the sons of the Levites: the Levites themselves
decisions.reason: "Sons of" here marks members of the group, as in "sons of Israel". The Levites are meant, not their children.

decisions.choice: the poles: carrying poles
decisions.reason: The word means a bar or pole for carrying a load on the shoulders. Exodus uses a different word for the ark's poles, but the same objects are meant.

decisions.choice: the Levites carried the ark: told ahead of the procession itself
decisions.reason: The verse sums up what happened before verses 16-24 list the musicians and gatekeepers; the procession itself is told in verses 25-29.

decisions.choice: on their shoulders with the poles, as Moses had commanded
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the description of how they carried the ark together and put Moses' command at the end. Readable makes the LORD's word a sentence of its own.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִיד֮ לְשָׂרֵ֣י הַלְוִיִּם֒ לְהַֽעֲמִ֗יד אֶת־אֲחֵיהֶם֙ הַמְשֹׁ֣רְרִ֔ים בִּכְלֵי־שִׁ֛יר נְבָלִ֥ים וְכִנֹּר֖וֹת וּמְצִלְתָּ֑יִם מַשְׁמִיעִ֥ים לְהָרִֽים־בְּק֖וֹל לְשִׂמְחָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And said David to [the] chiefs of the Levites to appoint their brothers the singers with instruments of song, harps and lyres and cymbals, sounding aloud, to raise with [a] sound for joy.

en.L: And David told the chiefs of the Levites to appoint their brothers [as] the singers, with instruments of song, harps and lyres and cymbals, sounding aloud, to raise [the] sound for joy.
en.B: David also told the chiefs of the Levites to appoint some of their relatives as singers, with musical instruments, harps, lyres and cymbals, to play loudly and raise sounds of joy.
en.R: David also told the leaders of the Levites to choose some of their relatives to be singers. They were to play harps, lyres and cymbals loudly and make joyful music.

decisions.choice: harps: a larger stringed instrument
decisions.reason: The word names a stringed instrument larger than the lyre, probably a harp or a kind of large lyre. Its exact shape is not known.

decisions.choice: lyres: the smaller stringed instrument David played
decisions.reason: This is the instrument David played for Saul (1 Samuel 16:23), a lyre with a wooden frame. The two stringed instruments are named together, as in 2 Samuel 6:5.

decisions.choice: cymbals: a pair of metal plates struck together
decisions.reason: The word has the form used for pairs of things. Verse 19 says they were of bronze.

decisions.choice: David appoints the singers: the start of the Levite music for worship
decisions.reason: Chronicles tells that David set Levites over the music of the LORD's house (6:16-17), and later kings followed his order (2 Chronicles 29:25). The Levites who had carried the tabernacle now have a new work of praise.

decisions.choice: sounding aloud, to raise a sound for joy: playing loudly in celebration
decisions.reason: The first verb means to make heard; the second means to lift up. Together they describe loud music and singing for joy.

decisions.choice: some of their relatives
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "some of", since verses 17-24 show that only some of the Levites were made singers. "Relatives" is "brothers" as in verse 5.

source.text: וַיַּעֲמִ֣ידוּ הַלְוִיִּ֗ם אֵ֚ת הֵימָ֣ן בֶּן־יוֹאֵ֔ל וּמִ֨ן־אֶחָ֔יו אָסָ֖ף בֶּן־בֶּֽרֶכְיָ֑הוּסוּמִן־בְּנֵ֤י מְרָרִי֙ אֲחֵיהֶ֔ם אֵיתָ֖ן בֶּן־קֽוּשָׁיָֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And appointed the Levites Heman son of Joel, and of his brothers Asaph son of Berechiah, and of [the] sons of Merari their brothers Ethan son of Kushaiah.

en.L: And the Levites appointed Heman the son of Joel, and from his brothers, Asaph the son of Berechiah, and from the sons of Merari their brothers, Ethan the son of Kushaiah.
en.B: So the Levites appointed Heman son of Joel; from his relatives, Asaph son of Berechiah; and from their relatives the descendants of Merari, Ethan son of Kushaiah.
en.R: So the Levites chose Heman son of Joel. From his relatives they chose Asaph son of Berechiah. And from the clan of Merari, who were also their relatives, they chose Ethan son of Kushaiah.

decisions.choice: Heman, Asaph and Ethan: the three heads of the singers
decisions.reason: The family lists in 6:18-32 trace Heman to Kohath (6:18-23), Asaph to Gershom (6:24-28) and Ethan to Merari (6:29-32), so each of Levi's three clans has a leader of song. Psalms carry the names of Asaph (Psalms 50; 73-83), Heman (Psalm 88) and Ethan (Psalm 89).

decisions.choice: Kushaiah: called Kishi in 6:29
decisions.reason: Ethan's father is Kishi in 6:29 and Kushaiah here; they are two forms of one name. Later lists name Jeduthun beside Heman and Asaph (16:41-42; 25:1), and he may be the same man as Ethan.

decisions.choice: chose
decisions.reason: Readable says "chose" for "appointed", as in verse 16.

source.text: וְעִמָּהֶ֖ם אֲחֵיהֶ֣ם הַמִּשְׁנִ֑ים זְכַרְיָ֡הוּ בֵּ֡ן וְיַֽעֲזִיאֵ֡ל וּשְׁמִֽירָמ֡וֹת וִיחִיאֵ֣ל׀וְעֻנִּ֡י אֱלִיאָ֡ב וּבְנָיָ֡הוּ וּמַֽעֲשֵׂיָ֡הוּ וּמַתִּתְיָהוּ֩ וֶאֱלִ֨יפְלֵ֜הוּ וּמִקְנֵיָ֨הוּ וְעֹבֵ֥ד אֱדֹ֛ם וִֽיעִיאֵ֖ל הַשֹּׁעֲרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And with them their brothers the second [rank]: Zechariah, Ben and Jaaziel and Shemiramoth and Jehiel and Unni, Eliab and Benaiah and Maaseiah and Mattithiah and Eliphelehu and Mikneiah and Obed-Edom and Jeiel the gatekeepers.

en.L: And with them [were] their brothers of the second [rank]: Zechariah, Ben and Jaaziel and Shemiramoth and Jehiel and Unni, Eliab and Benaiah and Maaseiah and Mattithiah and Eliphelehu and Mikneiah, and Obed-Edom and Jeiel, the gatekeepers.
en.B: With them were their relatives of the second rank: Zechariah, Ben, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu and Mikneiah, and the gatekeepers Obed-Edom and Jeiel.
en.R: Working with them were relatives who were next in rank: Zechariah, Ben, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu and Mikneiah. Obed-Edom and Jeiel, who were gatekeepers, were also with them.

decisions.choice: the second rank: assistants to the three leaders
decisions.reason: The word means "second" or "next in order". These men served under Heman, Asaph and Ethan, and verses 20-21 give their instruments.

decisions.choice: Ben: kept as a name, as the Hebrew text has it
alternatives: leave Ben out, as the Greek does
decisions.reason: "Ben" is the word for "son", and a man called simply Ben is found nowhere else. He is missing from the same list in verse 20, and the Greek translation does not have him. The word may be left over from a phrase such as "Zechariah son of ..." in copying. The Hebrew text is kept here.

decisions.choice: the gatekeepers: Obed-Edom and Jeiel
decisions.reason: The title belongs to the last two names. Obed-Edom is a gatekeeper again in verse 24 and 16:38, and in verse 21 he also plays the lyre. Whether he is the Obed-Edom at whose house the ark stayed (13:13-14) is not said; 26:4-8 lists the gatekeeper's large family as a sign of God's blessing.

decisions.choice: the gatekeepers Obed-Edom and Jeiel
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the title before the two names so that it is not read as applying to the whole list; Readable makes them a sentence of their own.

source.text: וְהַמְשֹׁ֣רְרִ֔ים הֵימָ֥ן אָסָ֖ף וְאֵיתָ֑ן בִּמְצִלְתַּ֥יִם נְחֹ֖שֶׁת לְהַשְׁמִֽיעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the singers, Heman, Asaph and Ethan, with cymbals of bronze to sound aloud.

en.L: And the singers, Heman, Asaph and Ethan, [were] with bronze cymbals, to sound aloud.
en.B: The singers Heman, Asaph and Ethan were to play bronze cymbals loudly.
en.R: The singers Heman, Asaph and Ethan were to play loud bronze cymbals.

decisions.choice: the leaders with cymbals
decisions.reason: The three leaders play the cymbals, perhaps to set the beat or to mark the start and end of the songs. Asaph has the cymbals again in 16:5.

decisions.choice: to sound aloud: to make the music heard
decisions.reason: As in verse 16, the verb means "to make heard".

decisions.choice: were to play
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the verb the Hebrew leaves out.

source.text: וּזְכַרְיָ֨ה וַעֲזִיאֵ֜ל וּשְׁמִֽירָמ֤וֹת וִֽיחִיאֵל֙ וְעֻנִּ֣י וֶֽאֱלִיאָ֔ב וּמַעֲשֵׂיָ֖הוּ וּבְנָיָ֑הוּ בִּנְבָלִ֖ים עַל־עֲלָמֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And Zechariah and Aziel and Shemiramoth and Jehiel and Unni and Eliab and Maaseiah and Benaiah with harps on alamoth.

en.L: And Zechariah and Aziel and Shemiramoth and Jehiel and Unni and Eliab and Maaseiah and Benaiah [were] with harps, on alamoth.
en.B: Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah and Benaiah were to play harps, on alamoth.
en.R: Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah and Benaiah were to play harps for high voices.

decisions.choice: on alamoth: a musical term, perhaps "for high voices"
alternatives: a tune or instrument whose name is lost
decisions.reason: The word is the plural of the word for a young woman, and it heads Psalm 46. It is a musical direction, perhaps for high voices or instruments set to a high pitch, but its exact sense is no longer known.

decisions.choice: Aziel: the Jaaziel of verse 18
decisions.reason: The list repeats the first eight names of verse 18, with Aziel for Jaaziel (two forms of one name), without Ben, and with Maaseiah before Benaiah.

decisions.choice: on alamoth (Literal, Balanced); for high voices (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Psalm 46:1, Literal and Balanced keep the term and Readable gives its likeliest sense (m1).

source.text: וּמַתִּתְיָ֣הוּ וֶאֱלִֽיפְלֵ֗הוּ וּמִקְנֵיָ֨הוּ֙ וְעֹבֵ֣ד אֱדֹ֔ם וִֽיעִיאֵ֖ל וַעֲזַזְיָ֑הוּ בְּכִנֹּר֥וֹת עַל־הַשְּׁמִינִ֖ית לְנַצֵּֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And Mattithiah and Eliphelehu and Mikneiah and Obed-Edom and Jeiel and Azaziah with lyres on the sheminith to lead.

en.L: And Mattithiah and Eliphelehu and Mikneiah and Obed-Edom and Jeiel and Azaziah [were] with lyres, on the sheminith, to lead.
en.B: Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, Jeiel and Azaziah were to lead with lyres, on the sheminith.
en.R: Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, Jeiel and Azaziah were to lead the music on lyres, set to "the eighth".

decisions.choice: the sheminith: "the eighth", a musical term
decisions.reason: The word means "the eighth" and heads Psalms 6 and 12. It may name a pitch, a tune or an instrument, perhaps a lower pitch set against the alamoth of verse 20; its sense is no longer known.

decisions.choice: to lead: to direct the music
decisions.reason: The verb means to oversee or lead. The same word stands in the heading "for the director" at the start of many psalms (Psalm 4:1).

decisions.choice: Azaziah: a name not in verse 18
decisions.reason: The six names repeat the last six of verse 18 and add Azaziah.

decisions.choice: on the sheminith (Literal, Balanced); set to "the eighth" (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Psalm 6:1, Literal and Balanced keep the term and Readable translates the word.

source.text: וּכְנַנְיָ֥הוּ שַֽׂר־הַלְוִיִּ֖ם בְּמַשָּׂ֑א יָסֹר֙ בַּמַּשָּׂ֔א כִּ֥י מֵבִ֖ין הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And Chenaniah, chief of the Levites in lifting up, instructing in the lifting up, for skilled [was] he.

en.L: And Chenaniah, chief of the Levites in the lifting up [of song], instructed in the lifting up [of song], for he [was] skilled.
en.B: Chenaniah, the chief of the Levites in charge of the music, directed the music, because he was skilled at it.
en.R: Chenaniah, a leader of the Levites, was in charge of the music. He directed it because he was skilled at it.

decisions.choice: the lifting up: the music, the lifting up of voices in song
alternatives: in charge of the carrying (of the ark)
in charge of the prophetic utterance
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "lift, carry". It can mean a load that is carried, an utterance lifted up as in a prophet's message, or the raising of the voice in song. Since Chenaniah is named among the singers in verse 27 and is "skilled", the music is the likeliest sense here. But the chapter is about carrying the ark (verses 2, 15, 26-27), and he may have directed the carrying.

decisions.choice: instructed: directed, trained the others
decisions.reason: The form is unusual. It is most likely from the verb "instruct, discipline", so he taught and directed the others; it may also be read as a form of "be chief", "he was in charge".

decisions.choice: skilled: one who understood the work
decisions.reason: The word means "understanding". In 25:7-8 it is used of trained musicians and their teachers.

decisions.choice: [of song]
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "lifting up" and supplies what is lifted, as m1 reads it. Balanced and Readable say "the music".

source.text: וּבֶֽרֶכְיָה֙ וְאֶלְקָנָ֔ה שֹׁעֲרִ֖ים לָאָרֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And Berechiah and Elkanah [were] gatekeepers for the ark.

en.L: And Berechiah and Elkanah [were] gatekeepers for the ark.
en.B: Berechiah and Elkanah were gatekeepers for the ark.
en.R: Berechiah and Elkanah were gatekeepers who guarded the ark.

decisions.choice: gatekeepers for the ark: guards for the ark and its tent
decisions.reason: Gatekeepers kept watch at the entrances of the sanctuary and controlled who came in (9:17-27). Here they guard the ark on its way and at its new tent.

decisions.choice: who guarded the ark
decisions.reason: Readable says what gatekeepers did for the ark.

source.text: וּשְׁבַנְיָ֡הוּ וְיֽוֹשָׁפָ֡ט וּנְתַנְאֵ֡ל וַעֲמָשַׂ֡י וּ֠זְכַרְיָהוּ וּבְנָיָ֤הוּ וֶֽאֱלִיעֶ֨זֶר֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים מַחְצְרִים֙ בַּחֲצֹ֣צְר֔וֹת לִפְנֵ֖י אֲר֣וֹן הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְעֹבֵ֤ד אֱדֹם֙ וִֽיחִיָּ֔ה שֹׁעֲרִ֖ים לָאָרֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And Shebaniah and Joshaphat and Nethanel and Amasai and Zechariah and Benaiah and Eliezer the priests blowing on the trumpets before [the] ark of the God; and Obed-Edom and Jehiah gatekeepers for the ark.

en.L: And Shebaniah and Joshaphat and Nethanel and Amasai and Zechariah and Benaiah and Eliezer, the priests, [were] blowing the trumpets before the ark of God; and Obed-Edom and Jehiah [were] gatekeepers for the ark.
en.B: Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah and Eliezer, who were priests, were to sound the trumpets in front of the ark of God. Obed-Edom and Jehiah were gatekeepers for the ark as well.
en.R: The priests Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah and Eliezer were to blow trumpets in front of the ark of God. Obed-Edom and Jehiah were also gatekeepers who guarded the ark.

decisions.choice: the priests blowing the trumpets
decisions.reason: The law gave the two silver trumpets to the priests, to be blown for gatherings, for battle and at festivals and offerings (Numbers 10:1-10). They were different from the ram's horn of verse 28.

decisions.choice: blowing the trumpets: the verb is spelled two ways
decisions.reason: The letters written in the text and the reading noted in the margin of the Hebrew Bible give two spellings of the verb "blow trumpets". Both mean the same.

decisions.choice: Obed-Edom and Jehiah: a second pair of gatekeepers
decisions.reason: Jehiah may be the Jeiel named with Obed-Edom in verses 18 and 21, under another form of the name, but the text does not say.

decisions.choice: as well (Balanced); also (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "as well" or "also" to link these gatekeepers with those in verse 23. Readable says what they did, as in verse 23.

source.text: וַיְהִ֥י דָוִ֛יד וְזִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְשָׂרֵ֣י הָאֲלָפִ֑ים הַהֹֽלְכִ֗ים לְֽהַעֲל֞וֹת אֶת־אֲר֧וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָ֛ה מִן־בֵּ֥ית עֹבֵֽד־אֱדֹ֖ם בְּשִׂמְחָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And it was David and [the] elders of Israel and [the] commanders of the thousands, the [ones] going to bring up [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh from [the] house of Obed-Edom with joy.

en.L: And it was David and the elders of Israel and the commanders of thousands who went to bring up the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the house of Obed-Edom with rejoicing.
en.B: So David and the elders of Israel and the commanders of thousands went to bring the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} up from the house of Obed-Edom with rejoicing.
en.R: So David, the elders of Israel and the commanders of the army's units of a thousand went with great joy to bring the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s covenant up from Obed-Edom's house.

decisions.choice: verses 25-29 retell 2 Samuel 6:12-16
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 6:12 says that David went after hearing how the LORD had blessed Obed-Edom's house (that blessing is told in 13:14). Chronicles names the elders and the commanders with David, says "the ark of the covenant of the LORD" for "the ark of God", and does not name the city of David here.

decisions.choice: commanders of thousands: the army's officers
decisions.reason: These were the officers over the army's large units, who had taken part in the decision to bring the ark (13:1).

decisions.choice: with rejoicing: with open celebration
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 6:12: joy shown with music, shouting and dancing (verses 28-29).

decisions.choice: the commanders of the army's units of a thousand
decisions.reason: Readable says what "commanders of thousands" were (m2), and, as Deuteronomy 10:8 does, puts the ark of the covenant as "the ark of the LORD's covenant".

source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ בֶּעְזֹ֣ר הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶ֨ת־הַלְוִיִּ֔ם נֹשְׂאֵ֖י אֲר֣וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּזְבְּח֥וּ שִׁבְעָֽה־פָרִ֖ים וְשִׁבְעָ֥ה אֵילִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when helped the God the Levites carrying [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh, and they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.

en.L: And it happened, when God helped the Levites who were carrying the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [that] they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.
en.B: When God helped the Levites carrying the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, they offered seven bulls and seven rams in sacrifice.
en.R: As the Levites carried the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s covenant, God helped them, and they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.

decisions.choice: the sacrifice on the way: compare 2 Samuel 6:13
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 6:13 says that when the carriers had gone six steps, David sacrificed an ox and a fattened animal. Chronicles says God helped the Levites, and "they" sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.

decisions.choice: God helped the Levites: they came to no harm
decisions.reason: On the first attempt the LORD broke out against Uzzah (13:10-11). This time the ark was carried as the law required, and God kept the carriers safe; the sacrifices give thanks for it.

decisions.choice: when God helped: the time, and also the reason
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins "in" to the verb "help", which marks the time ("when") and can also give the reason ("because").

decisions.choice: seven bulls and seven rams: a full, generous offering
decisions.reason: Seven stands for completeness. Seven bulls and seven rams are offered in Job 42:8 and at the festival in Ezekiel 45:23.

decisions.choice: As the Levites carried ..., God helped them
decisions.reason: Readable starts with the carrying and joins the clauses with "and", which keeps both the sense of time and of reason (m3).

source.text: וְדָוִ֞יד מְכֻרְבָּ֣ל׀בִּמְעִ֣יל בּ֗וּץ וְכָל־הַלְוִיִּם֙ הַנֹּשְׂאִ֣ים אֶת־הָאָר֔וֹן וְהַמְשֹׁ֣רְרִ֔ים וּכְנַנְיָ֛ה הַשַּׂ֥ר הַמַּשָּׂ֖א הַמְשֹֽׁרְרִ֑ים וְעַל־דָּוִ֖יד אֵפ֥וֹד בָּֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And David [was] wrapped in a robe of fine linen, and all the Levites carrying the ark, and the singers, and Chenaniah the chief [of] the lifting up [of] the singers; and on David [was an] ephod of linen.

en.L: And David [was] clothed in a robe of fine linen, and [so were] all the Levites who were carrying the ark, and the singers, and Chenaniah the chief of the lifting up [of song] of the singers; and on David [was] a linen ephod.
en.B: David was dressed in a robe of fine linen, and so were all the Levites carrying the ark, the singers and Chenaniah, who led the music of the singers. David also wore a linen ephod.
en.R: David was wearing a robe made of fine linen. So were all the Levites who carried the ark, and the singers, and Chenaniah, the leader of the singers' music. David also wore a linen ephod, a simple garment like the ones priests wore.

decisions.choice: clothed in a robe of fine linen: compare 2 Samuel 6:14
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 6:14 reads "David was whirling with all his strength before the LORD". Chronicles has "David was clothed in a robe of fine linen". In Hebrew the two verbs for "whirling" and "clothed" look much alike. Chronicles dresses David like the Levites around him; his dancing comes in verse 29. Both accounts end the verse with the linen ephod.

decisions.choice: clothed: wrapped
decisions.reason: The verb is found only here. It is linked with a word for a garment or cloak found in Aramaic (Daniel 3:21).

decisions.choice: fine linen and a linen ephod: the dress of those who served in worship
decisions.reason: The Levite singers wore fine linen at the temple's dedication (2 Chronicles 5:12). The linen ephod was the plain garment of those who served at the sanctuary (1 Samuel 2:18; 22:18), as in 2 Samuel 6:14.

decisions.choice: the lifting up of the singers: the music, as in verse 22
decisions.reason: The same uncertain word as in verse 22. The Hebrew is very compressed here: "the chief, the lifting up, the singers".

decisions.choice: [so were]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the words that show the Levites, singers and Chenaniah were dressed the same way.

decisions.choice: a simple garment like the ones priests wore
decisions.reason: Readable explains the ephod, as in 2 Samuel 6:14.

source.text: וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מַעֲלִים֙ אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָ֔ה בִּתְרוּעָה֙ וּבְק֣וֹל שׁוֹפָ֔ר וּבַחֲצֹצְר֖וֹת וּבִמְצִלְתָּ֑יִם מַשְׁמִעִ֕ים בִּנְבָלִ֖ים וְכִנֹּרֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And all Israel bringing up [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh with shouting and with [the] sound of [the] ram's horn and with trumpets and with cymbals, sounding aloud with harps and lyres.

en.L: And all Israel [were] bringing up the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with shouting and with the sound of the ram's horn, and with trumpets and with cymbals, sounding aloud with harps and lyres.
en.B: So all Israel brought the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} up with loud shouts of joy and the sound of the ram's horn, with trumpets and cymbals, and with the loud music of harps and lyres.
en.R: So all Israel brought the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s covenant up to the city. They shouted with joy, and the ram's horn was blown. Trumpets and cymbals sounded, and harps and lyres played loudly.

decisions.choice: compare 2 Samuel 6:15
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 6:15 has "David and all the house of Israel" bringing up "the ark of the LORD" with shouting and the ram's horn. Chronicles has "all Israel" and "the ark of the covenant of the LORD", and adds the trumpets, cymbals, harps and lyres of the musicians listed in verses 16-24.

decisions.choice: shouting: a loud shout of acclaim
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 6:15: the joyful shout that greets a king or the LORD.

decisions.choice: the ram's horn and the trumpets
decisions.reason: The ram's horn (shofar) was blown for signals and holy days; the trumpets were the priests' metal trumpets (verse 24).

decisions.choice: shouts of joy
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 6:15. Readable adds "to the city", as there, and breaks the verse into short sentences.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י אֲרוֹן֙ בְּרִ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה בָּ֖א עַד־עִ֣יר דָּוִ֑יד וּמִיכַ֨ל בַּת־שָׁא֜וּל נִשְׁקְפָ֣ה׀בְּעַ֣ד הַחַלּ֗וֹן וַתֵּ֨רֶא אֶת־הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ דָּוִיד֙ מְרַקֵּ֣ד וּמְשַׂחֵ֔ק וַתִּ֥בֶז ל֖וֹ בְּלִבָּֽהּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And it was, [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh came to [the] city of David, and Michal [the] daughter of Saul looked down through the window and saw the king David dancing and making merry, and she despised him in her heart.

en.L: And it happened, [as] the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to the city of David, Michal the daughter of Saul looked down through the window and saw King David dancing and making merry, and she despised him in her heart.
en.B: As the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was coming into the city of David, Michal the daughter of Saul looked down from the window. She saw King David dancing and celebrating, and in her heart she despised him.
en.R: As the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s covenant was coming into the city of David, Saul's daughter Michal looked out of a window. She saw King David dancing and celebrating, and in her heart she despised him.

decisions.choice: dancing and making merry: compare 2 Samuel 6:16
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 6:16 has David "leaping and whirling before the LORD". Chronicles uses two other verbs, "dancing" (skipping, as in Ecclesiastes 3:4) and "making merry" (the verb of 13:8 and 2 Samuel 6:5), and does not have "before the LORD". It also says "the ark of the covenant of the LORD". The rest of the verse is the same.

decisions.choice: Michal the daughter of Saul
decisions.reason: Michal was David's wife (1 Samuel 18:27). Naming her as Saul's daughter recalls the house of Saul, whose rule the LORD had turned over to David (10:13-14). Chronicles does not tell her quarrel with David (2 Samuel 6:20-23); the story goes on in 16:1.

decisions.choice: despised him: looked on him with contempt
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 6:16: she counted his behavior unworthy of a king.

decisions.choice: celebrating
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "celebrating" for "making merry". The rest follows the wording of 2 Samuel 6:16.
